register.name: Intergenerational Trust Fund for the People of the Republic of Nauru
register.detail: Government of Nauru · established 6 November 2015 · asset holdings A$412M in May 2025 · government contribution A$22.6M in FY2025 · IMF staff report, September 2025
register.note: Australia, New Zealand and Taiwan have memoranda with the fund; Taiwan is exiting it, according to IMF staff
register.text: A trust fund owned by the people of Nauru and built from government and partner contributions, which begins distributions when its committee determines that it has reached its target value. IMF staff put its asset holdings at A$412 million in May 2025, about one and a half times the GDP of FY2025. It is the long-term buffer of the public finances on which the seven standards depend.

register.name: Development Fund Projection, 2025–26
register.detail: Government of Nauru · presented to Parliament 29 August 2025 · A$50M direct budget support and A$107.2M in kind · Australia A$44.9M, Japan A$31.2M, China A$46M, ADB A$18.9M, United Nations A$11.9M, New Zealand A$4.8M
register.note: Includes A$6.5 million for the HIV/TB Programme and A$2.6 million for the urban water, sanitation and waste project
register.text: The support that Nauru’s development partners pledged for the 2025–26 financial year, as presented to Parliament by the President and Minister for Finance. It combines direct budget support from Australia and China with in-kind projects for health and education, water, sanitation, solar power and the port, which serve the water, health, education and energy standards and the public finances.

register.name: Sustainable and Climate Resilient Connectivity for Nauru (FP052)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · accredited entity the Asian Development Bank · approved 2 October 2017 · GCF financing $26.91M of a $65.2M project · new wharf, fuel pipeline and southern container yard operational
register.note: Aiwo Port is the country’s main gateway for imports and exports, according to ADB
register.text: Climate finance from the Green Climate Fund for a climate-resilient port at Aiwo, built with the Asian Development Bank. Nauru depends significantly on its port for supplies of food, energy and most other essentials, so a port that withstands the weather protects the food and energy standards.

register.name: Grant to strengthen the public finances, with support for fuel, shipping and import costs
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · grant · news release of 17 November 2026 · includes $3.56M of additional support for rising fuel, shipping and import costs
register.note: ADB attributes the higher fuel, shipping and import costs to the Middle East conflict
register.text: A grant from the Asian Development Bank to help Nauru strengthen its public finances, including $3.56 million of additional support to cope with rising fuel, shipping and import costs caused by the Middle East conflict. It protects public spending on the seven standards when the prices of imported fuel and food rise.

register.name: Sustainable and Resilient Urban Development Project
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · Asian Development Fund grant 0970-NAU · approved 27 September 2024 · effective 4 December 2025 · Government of Nauru $2.3M · no civil works contract awarded by 31 December 2025
register.note: Nauru’s first reticulated water supply, planned to reach 55% of the population
register.text: A grant from the Asian Development Fund for Nauru’s first piped water network of tanks, pumps and pipes, wider access to desalinated water, improved sanitation with septage treatment, and an organic waste composting facility. It serves the water standard, the furthest from reach in Nauru, and the shelter standard through sanitation.

register.name: Solar Power Development Project
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · grant 0664 · Pacific Renewable Energy Investment Facility · Government of Nauru $4.98M · 6 MW solar plant with a 5 MW / 2.5 MWh battery · solar arrays energised and integrated into the grid 1 December 2025
register.note: Operating at reduced capacity until the control system and the battery are fully online, ADB reported in March 2026
register.text: A grant from the Asian Development Bank for a 6-megawatt grid-connected solar plant with battery storage on four hectares of Nauru’s plateau, reducing the island’s reliance on imported diesel for power. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Australian development assistance, 2026–27
register.detail: Australian Government · total ODA budget estimate 2026–27 · country program A$25.9M · regional A$19.6M · DFAT fact sheet, May 2026
register.note: Economic infrastructure and services take 36% of the 2026–27 programme, education 12% and health 9%
register.text: Australia’s total official development assistance to Nauru in its 2026–27 development budget, 0.9% of Australia’s total aid. The programme supports health, education, sport, infrastructure and economic governance, which serve the health and education standards and the public finances.
by: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

register.name: Budget support from China, 2025–26
register.detail: People’s Republic of China · A$30M of budget support and A$16M in kind · Development Fund Projection 2025–26, presented to Parliament 29 August 2025
register.note: In-kind support covers infrastructure for the 2026 Micronesian Games, medical visits and consultations, tertiary scholarships and South-South cooperation
register.text: Direct budget support pledged by China for Nauru’s 2025–26 financial year, the larger of the two budget support contributions in the Development Fund Projection. Its in-kind support adds medical visits and consultations and tertiary scholarships, which bear on the health and education standards.

register.name: Nauru-Australia Treaty
register.detail: Australia · signed 9 December 2024 · in force 19 September 2025 · A$100M budget support and A$40M for policing and security, over five years
register.note: A$20 million of the budget support is in Nauru’s 2025–26 Development Fund Projection
register.text: An integrated economic, social and security partnership under which Australia provides A$100 million of budget support over five years for Nauru’s long-term investments and A$40 million for policing and security, and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia provides banking services in Nauru. Its budget support sustains the public finances on which the seven standards depend.

register.name: New Zealand International Development Cooperation, 2024–27
register.detail: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade · approved funding for 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2027 · plan target for Nauru
register.note: In 2025–26 New Zealand support totalled A$4.8 million, according to the Government of Nauru
register.text: New Zealand’s approved development cooperation for Nauru over the three years to June 2027. In 2025–26 it supported the Intergenerational Trust Fund, education support in Nauru and tertiary scholarships, which serve the education standard and the public finances.
by: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
